newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Tutu dubbed "weeping clown".
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Tutu dubbed "weeping clown".

text.p: South African Nobel peace laureate Archbishop Desmond Tutu was called "a weeping clown" on Thursday in a heated parliamentary debate on charges that his truth commission favours the ruling African National Congress.

"The Truth and Reconciliation Commission has become a sensationalist circus of horrors presided over by a weeping clown craving for the front stage spotlight," said Mangaqa Mncwango, a member of the opposition Inkatha Freedom Party.

"We have sent into the world a monster which is failing to heal the old wounds and is opening new ones ... We cannot escape our responsibility to shut down the commission before it causes irreparable damage," he said.
Members of the ANC objected to Mncwango's remarks about Tutu, chairman of the commission, and the speaker ordered him to withdraw them.
Mncwango said Tutu had for many years been biased in favour of the ANC, accusing him of turning a cold shoulder to Inkatha when it complained of ANC attacks on its members.
The debate was called after the National Party (NP) of former president F.W. de Klerk clashed with Tutu over the way he conducted hearings for political parties last week.
The NP, which is boycotting the commission, accused it of treating the ANC with kid gloves and of prematurely deciding that de Klerk's government had been guilty of atrocities during apartheid.
Tutu said last week he had come close to tears when de Klerk told the commission he did not know how widespread torture and murder had become by the apartheid police.
The archbishop has previously wept during testimony to the commission by victims of torture.
